key_insight: Creative AI should not be judged by forcing experts to agree. The Human Creativity Benchmark separates shared professional standards from legitimate differences in taste, so evaluation can capture both consensus and subjective preference.
problem_solved: Current AI evaluation methods often treat evaluator disagreement as random error, which breaks down in creative tasks where disagreement can be meaningful. This paper addresses how to evaluate creative AI without losing the signal in human disagreement.
method: Defines two distinct evaluation signals: convergence, where experts agree on best practices, and divergence, where expert opinions legitimately vary.
Creates the Human Creativity Benchmark (HCB) to preserve and measure both signals separately.
Frames evaluator disagreement as structured evidence rather than noise in creative-domain assessment.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a more realistic way to evaluate generative and creative systems. It can improve benchmark design, reduce misleading metrics, and better reflect how humans actually judge creative work.
